items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: Because I remember one time that Illinois Jacquet was in the band, and he got sick or something and he was out for two or three days.

ctx.x: Yeah. I had to take a back seat to Ben. And it disturbed me a little bit, because I wasn't playing no more solos. The only solos I got a chance to play was the sweet solos, which I made the arrangements. So I went back and told Merle. He said, "Well, man, don't worry about that." He said, "You've been playing them solos all these years. And remember, every time another guy is playing a solo, you're resting." It made sense. So I just started enjoying hearing Ben and anybody else play.

And another thing they couldn't understand. If any of the saxophone players that was playing their solos was out for some reason or another, I could play the solos. Because I remember one time that Illinois Jacquet was in the band, and he got sick or something and he was out for two or three days. We was playing in one of them big clubs over there in Jersey. And when his solo come up, I just played his solo. Because I'd sat down and listened to the chord structure. All I needed to know was the chord structure.…
